prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer looks down at the ground (dark grey/black, ~1.2–1.5 m below), flanked by a person in an olive jacket on the left (~0.2–0.6 m away) and a person in a grey jacket on the right (~0.5–0.9 m away), spaced about 0.3–0.5 m apart and facing inward toward the center with their heads cropped out above the frame. Within arm's reach at the bottom center (~0.3–0.5 m from the lens), the camera wearer's left hand and an open rectangular storage case sit at mid-bright values directly between and below both bystanders. Across the five frames, an overhanging object at the top center disappears after frame 1, the left person's raised arm in the upper-left corner remains extremely close (bright white, ~0.15–0.25 m), the camera wearer's left hand rises slightly while holding a small device in frames 2–5, and the right person's right arm extends downward and closer in frames 4–5 to meet the camera wearer's hand over the case. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the steep vertical layering between the raised foreground arm on the left, the mid-level hands and case, the right person's receding torso, and the distant pavement. However, the map is unreliable inside the open storage case—where individual small batteries and compartments are smoothed into a flat planar blob—and along the upper-left sleeve in frames 4–5 where brightness saturates and bleeds across object boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels two primary 'person' regions facing inward—the person on the left in brown (~0.2–0.6 m away, partially occluded by the left and bottom frame edges) and the person on the right in light pink (~0.5–0.9 m away, partially out of view at the top and right edges)—separated by a narrow strip of unlabelled black pavement. At the bottom center within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer), the open equipment case and small electronic modules held between the camera wearer's hands and the right person's hands are segmented as small overlapping regions inframes 1–5. Across the sequence, the right person's pink mask retreats slightly at the top after frame 1 and then extends a narrow arm protrusion downward toward the bottom-center case in frames 4–5 to contact the object held by the camera wearer's left hand. While the map helps isolate the silhouettes of the two standing people from the textured pavement background, it is highly unreliable for objects and body ownership: it misclassifies the small camera batteries and the entire storage case as 'cell phone' instances, merges the camera wearer's own left hand and right forearm into the left person's brown mask, and loses the case entirely inside the person mask by frames 4–5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a yellow torso and arm skeleton for the person on the left (~0.3–0.6 m away, angled toward the center and right) alongside magenta 3D hand skeletons in the lower half of the frame (~0.3–0.5 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the right person). In frame 1, two magenta hand skeletons appear near the center—corresponding to the right person's left and right hands holding a device—while from frame 2 to frame 5 the tracked hands shift to the camera wearer's left hand at the bottom center and the right person's reaching right hand just above and to the right of it. Across frames 1 to 5, the two tracked magenta hands converge at the bottom center as the right person's right hand reaches down in frames 4–5 to grasp the small module from the camera wearer's left hand, while the yellow torso skeleton shifts upward and disappears completely in frame 5. The pose map reveals detailed finger articulation, pinch geometry, and wrist orientation during the handoff that are partially self-occluded in RGB. However, it is unreliable in overall scene coverage: it completely fails to detect the body skeleton of the person on the right, misses the right person's left hand after frame 1, fabricates spurious facial/head keypoints (yellow dots) on the left person's raised forearm even though all heads are out of view, and drops the left person's body skeleton in the final frame.
